text: OVER BLACK: A bell. One stroke. It does not fade. It hangs.
FADE IN:
1   INT. ORISON - CATHEDRAL OF THE ASCENSION - DAY                 1
White stone and light. Columns no thicker than a man climb two hundred feet into mist. Petals fall from the high galleries, too slowly.
SUPER: "THE KINGDOM OF ORISON. YEAR 800 OF THE ASCENSION."
Ten thousand guests in white, under the banners of the seven kingdoms. Beyond the arches there is no land and no horizon. Only cloud, and white warships at anchor in the air, every flag flying.
A BRIDE and GROOM kneel beneath an open tower. In it hangs a new bell, bronze, the size of a house, still slung in the chains of the fleet barge that lifted it. The HIEROPHANT (70s) raises his arms.

speaker: HIEROPHANT
text: Heaven chose us from the earth and raised us above the unworthy. What heaven has raised --

speaker: TEN THOUSAND VOICES
text: Let no hand bring down.

GRAND ADMIRAL SERATH (50s) stands among the admirals, a collar of heavy gold at her throat. Up here it weighs almost nothing. She watches the rite the way she would watch a harbour. At her shoulder: VICE ADMIRAL CASSIEL (60s), correct to the last button. He has wanted that collar for ten years.
A GIRL of seven, strewing petals, trips beside her. The basket leaves her hands and drifts. Serath takes it out of the air without looking, and gives it back.
An AIDE offers the day's lifting warrant and red wax. She presses her ring into the wax without reading. Her seal: an anchor in a ring of stars.

The aide lifts the sealed warrant toward the tower. Above it the barge lets go. Its chains fall slack. The bell settles onto the cathedral's own beam, and the kingdom takes its weight. A hammer the size of a door swings back.
The bell is struck.
CUT TO:
2   EXT. ANVIL VALE - A FIELD - DAY                                 2
SUPER: "ANVIL VALE."
Quiet. A low grey sky, and in it one darker shape that covers half of it. It has always been there.
Under the quiet, a hum too deep to hear. It is in the ground and in the teeth.
A FARMER (40s) works a furrow. Everything here is built to bear: the low stone house, buttressed like a fort; the ox's yoke; his own back. When he stands he does not straighten. Nobody here does.
His DAUGHTER (6) brings him water in a wooden bowl. He drinks and sets it on the wall. She keeps looking at it.
The water is trembling. Ring inside ring.
The ox drags at its rope. Crows leave the furrows and cannot climb. The farmer looks to the mountain the valley is named for. A line of dust has opened across its face. No sound yet.
Then the face of the mountain lets go.
He has the girl under his arm before the sound arrives. She has the bowl. The whole valley is running.
3   INT. ORISON - CATHEDRAL OF THE ASCENSION - CONTINUOUS           3
The bell's note is still in the air. Ten thousand gloved hands applaud, almost soundless. On a gallery rail stands a gold cup of wine. Its surface is perfectly still.
4   INT. ORISON - COUNCIL CHAMBER - DAY                             4
SUPER: "THREE DAYS LATER."
A gold cup on a white table. The wine in it is trembling. Ring inside ring. The CHANCELLOR (60s, tired, decent) cannot stop watching it.

A round room open to cloud. Outside, bells are ringing that no one has rung. Serath stands at an arch. Below her, cloud is rising through the lower terraces like a tide. Cassiel waits by the door, hands behind his back. An old ENGINEER has the floor, robes dusty to the knee.

speaker: ENGINEER
text: Six hundred feet since dawn. The Unrisen hold the Weir at Sarn. They are closing it against our weight.

speaker: HIEROPHANT
text: Then let it be broken.

speaker: ENGINEER
text: It would take every gun in the fleet. And -- Holiness, a Weir is a sluice, not a prop. Close it, and our weight backs up on us. Break it, and it pours. All of it, at once, onto the lowest ground. (he would rather not say it) Sarn Vale. It is not bearing-land. Nothing there is built for it. But we would hold our height.

speaker: SERATH
text: Forty thousand people live in Sarn Vale.

speaker: HIEROPHANT
text: And four million here. Heaven has done your arithmetic for you.

speaker: CHANCELLOR
text: I will not call it clean. I have grandchildren on the lower terraces. (to Serath) Break it.

speaker: SERATH
text: Give me until the evening bell. If they give back the Weir, nobody dies on either side. If they do not, I break it.

speaker: HIEROPHANT
text: Until the bell. If it finds the Weir standing, the fleet is Vice Admiral Cassiel's. (beat) And Admiral. Whatever they show you down there, remember who raised you.
She does not understand the warning. A clerk is already writing out the order. Cassiel waits for the seal before he inclines his head to her, perfectly courteous. She goes.
5   EXT. BENEATH ORISON - DAY                                         5

A naval cutter drops out of the cloud. Above it the underside of the kingdom fills the sky: raw rock, roots, chains thick as towers. Serath has never seen it from below. From here it is not beautiful. It is only enormous, and you can watch it sink.
Below: a plain of black basalt to the horizon, in columns, like a city no one finished.

At its edge, across the head of a green valley, stands THE WEIR, the ancient station that takes the weight of Orison. A mile of fused black stone without a seam or a tool-mark. Nine gates. Two are shut. Nothing visible pours through the others. But beneath them the grass lies combed flat, and a bird that crosses there drops like a stone.
Beyond it, SARN VALE. Terraces, orchards, the smoke of many hearths.
6   EXT. THE TREATY HOUSE - COURTYARD - DAY                           6
An old fort on the lip of the plain, older than either flag.

Serath steps from the cutter onto the ground. Her knees almost go. Behind her the aide falls outright. The gold collar drags at her neck like a hand. Surface soldiers watch the sky people learn to stand. Nobody laughs.
The yard is full of refugees, grey with rock dust. A woman in armour beaten from imperial hull-plate is handing out spears: MARL (30s), the dust of Anvil Vale still in her hair.
She puts one into the farmer's hands. He is alone. His free hand goes to the child's wooden bowl at his belt, and stays there.
They both watch the admiral pass. She notes the look, as she would note a gun, and does not know what it is.
KARST waits at the door. Fifties. Ink on his fingers. An imperial engineer's coat with the insignia cut away.

speaker: KARST
text: Admiral. You will want to sit down. Everyone does, the first time. (she does not) It is only your own weight. Down here that is a light day.

speaker: SERATH
text: You hold an imperial Weir. Return it by the evening bell and I will take your surrender on generous terms.

speaker: KARST
text: We did not attack your city, Admiral. We stopped carrying it.
7   INT. THE TREATY HOUSE - HALL - DAY                                7

Dark. One wall is a single face of basalt, cut with writing in two scripts, side by side. She can read one. It is the language of her prayers. Under both, worn almost flat, runs a third that belongs to neither people. The treaty was cut straight across it.
At its foot, two columns of seals. Seven crests she has saluted all her life. Beside them, eleven she has never seen. Cut the same size. Standing on the same line.

speaker: SERATH
text: "...the seven cities, raised by the hands of all, and borne by the nations of the high ground, until the fire is stone."
Karst shoulders the shutters open. Daylight. The black plain.

speaker: KARST
text: It was stone within forty years.

speaker: SERATH
text: We were chosen.

speaker: KARST
text: You were sheltered. (beat) By then you had gardens.
He holds a lamp over the floor. It is covered with paper: hundreds of lifting warrants, each held down by a stone. A hearthstone. A roof slate. The corner of a doorstep.
Every one carries the same seal. An anchor in a ring of stars.
She walks the rows. A dockyard. A battery. The Admiralty tower. Thirty years of her hand.

speaker: KARST
text: I drew where each one would fall. You sealed them.
The last stone is a grey shard, still shedding dust. She knows the wax. She knows the date.

speaker: SERATH
text: The marriage bell.

speaker: KARST
text: Ninety tons. Anvil Vale, the same hour. The bearing-lands have been full since before you were born. Every bell is a mountain now.
She takes off her glove and lays her bare hand on the shard. She leaves it there.

speaker: SERATH
text: I did not read it.

speaker: KARST
text: No one above reads them. That is how it was built. (beat) I read every one. And drew the next.
He turns back to the plain.

speaker: KARST
text: That will carry you. All of Orison. It is stone. It has no children. I can close the Weir a hand's breadth at a time and set you down as gently as you were lifted.

speaker: SERATH
text: And your price.

speaker: KARST
text: The fleet at anchor, colours struck. And the bearing-lands are no longer yours.

speaker: SERATH
text: You would have us fall.

speaker: KARST
text: No. We would have you come down.
Neither speaks for a while. Then she puts her glove back on.

speaker: SERATH
text: Four million people, disarmed, set down among eleven nations with every reason to hate them. What protects them?

speaker: KARST
text: Nothing. (beat) What has protected us?
He lets that stand. Then he lays a last sheet on her warrants. New paper. Along its foot, seals in grey wax.

speaker: KARST
text: A truce. No hand raised against anyone who comes down unarmed, until the harvest is in. After that I can promise you nothing. (she is counting the seals) Ten. The eleventh is in the courtyard, handing out spears. (the wall) We kept that eight hundred years. Read it.
She reads it. Every line.

speaker: SERATH
text: Give me time. I will put it to the Council --

speaker: KARST
text: We gave you time once. You are still spending it.
She folds the truce into her coat. Then she picks up the shard. He lets her.

speaker: SERATH
text: I will put it to them. If they refuse, I am still their admiral. Clear the vale by the evening bell.

speaker: KARST
text: "I am still their engineer." I said that for nineteen years. It is a comfortable sentence.
She walks out into her own weight.
8   EXT. THE PLAIN AND THE SKY ABOVE IT - DUSK                        8
The underside of the cloud, amber. Then it breaks in a thousand places.

The fleet of Orison comes down through it. White hulls like the naves of churches, rank above rank, until there is more ship than sky. Gunports open in long rows, with a sound like a city unlocking its doors.

From the flagship a lamp flashes up at the city: the terms and the truce, in clear. On every ship signalmen take them down, and officers read over their shoulders. Gun crews crowd the ports. Most have never seen the ground.
On the plain the armies of eleven nations look up. Spears. Old cannon. Farmers. Behind them the one road out of Sarn Vale is black with people.

At the Weir, the wheel that works the gates is forty feet across, its spokes worn bright by eight hundred years of hands. Fighters have their shoulders to it, Marl at their head. Karst stands at the lock-pin, one hand on it.

speaker: MARL
text: I dug for two days, Karst. My seal is not on your truce. (beat) All nine gates. All at once, before she fires. Let them learn it the way Anvil learned it.

speaker: KARST
text: She has not fired.
9   INT. FLAGSHIP - BRIDGE - DUSK                                     9
Brass, glass, quiet. Serath. Her FLAG CAPTAIN (40s). A hundred officers at their stations. Overhead, through the glass, the roots of Orison, lower than at noon.
On the rim of the city the Council's lamp is dark. She has been watching it for an hour. By her order every ship in the line has a glass on one road. The tally comes down the fleet, lamp to lamp.

speaker: FLAG CAPTAIN
text: The count, Admiral. Nine thousand clear of the vale. Of forty. (beat) They are carrying beds.
From far above, the evening bell. She bends to the sighting glass.
THROUGH THE GLASS: the Weir. The wheel. Karst, very small, looking up at her.

She swings down the valley. The road out of Sarn Vale, choked. Carts. Herds. A woman with a door on her back, because it is hers. They will not be clear by nightfall. They will not be clear by morning.
A small boy on his father's shoulders, shading his eyes, looking straight up. He seems to be looking at her.
ON THE BRIDGE, she straightens. In her left glove, the shard. The lamp on the rim has begun to flash. The flag captain reads it.

speaker: FLAG CAPTAIN
text: The Council's answer, Admiral. "What heaven has raised --"
He does not finish. Everyone on the bridge knows the rest.
Serath raises her right hand.
On every ship a signal arm rises with it. Ten thousand gunners watch. Silence. Even the bells have stopped.
AT THE WEIR, Marl throws her weight on the spoke. The wheel creaks. Karst does not take his hand from the pin.
ON THE BRIDGE, Serath's hand comes down. Not the chop that means fire. Slowly. Flat. Palm to the deck.

speaker: FLAG CAPTAIN
text: ...Guns, Admiral?

speaker: SERATH
text: Anchors.
Nobody moves. A lamp is flashing from the second ship of the line. The flag captain reads it without wanting to.

speaker: FLAG CAPTAIN
text: From Vice Admiral Cassiel. "The bell has rung. The Grand Admiral is relieved. The fleet fires on my signal."
He looks at the lamp. At his gunners. At her.
Serath unclasps the gold collar and lays it on the chart table.

speaker: SERATH
text: He is within the law. You know what this is called.

speaker: FLAG CAPTAIN
text: I know what it is called. (to the bridge) Let go all anchors.
10   EXT. THE PLAIN AND THE SKY ABOVE IT - DUSK                     10
From the flagship's keel an iron anchor falls on a mile of chain. It falls for a long time. It strikes the basalt. The sound comes late: one iron note, like a bell.
Nothing follows it.
A thousand ships hang where they are. On the second ship of the line a signal arm is still raised: Cassiel's. Every captain in the fleet can see them both.
Cassiel's arm drops. The chop that means fire.
Not one gun answers.

ON A GUN DECK down the line, a GUNNER (19): lanyard round his fist, the road he has counted in his sight. He looks at the next gunner, who is looking at him. Their lieutenant opens his mouth, and shuts it. Nobody will be first.
Then, far down the line, a small ship lets go its anchor. Then the one beside it. Then ten. Then the sky is raining iron, and when it stops there is a forest of chain between heaven and the ground.
The flagship's great white banner comes down its mast. Then the next ship's. Then the next. Not all. Here and there a ship keeps its colours and its height, and does nothing.
Cassiel's ship does not strike. It turns, alone, and climbs back into the cloud. Nobody fires on it.
AT THE WEIR the fighters take their shoulders from the spokes, one by one. Marl does not. She is watching the banners come down, and her face is doing something she has not given it leave to do.
She takes her hands off the wheel as if it burned.

speaker: MARL
text: I will not carry them. And I will not drop them.
She walks away along the Weir. A few follow her. Most stay. Karst draws the pin and sets his hands to the wheel.

speaker: KARST
text: Slowly.
The wheel turns, a hand's breadth at a time. Gate by gate, the Weir closes.
The cloud above the plain begins to tear.
A ceiling of rock, wider than the horizon. Roots. Chains. Then terraces streaming mist, bridges, hanging gardens, towers, and over them all the cathedral, its open tower holding the last of the sun.
A kingdom is coming down out of the sky. The sound is not loud. It is large. Every stone on the plain hums with it.
The armies of eleven nations have hated a shadow all their lives. Now they see what cast it. Some of them kneel. They do not mean to.

INSIDE ORISON: the banners of the cathedral, which have floated for eight hundred years, drop and hang straight. The hierophant, for the first time in his life, has to sit down. The chancellor stands at the arch with both hands on the stone. Below her, for the first time in hers, there is green.
ON THE PLAIN, the roots of Orison meet the black stone. The columns take the weight, and hold. Dust rolls out in a ring for miles. At the Weir the ninth gate closes.
Then the sound stops. All of it. The hum that has been in this ground for eight hundred years is gone, and nobody knew it was there until now.
11   EXT. THE PLAIN - LAST LIGHT                                       11
Silence.
A wall of white marble stands where this morning there was sky. Before it, very small, the soldiers of eleven nations do not know what to do with their hands.
Something is wrong with them. They are standing differently. All along the line, backs bent since birth are coming upright. A boy jumps, comes down late, laughs once, and stops.
The farmer unhooks the bowl and pours water into it from his flask.
The water does not move.
He looks at it for a long time. He is taller than he was this morning.

At the foot of an anchor chain Serath stands bare-throated in the dust, Karst beside her. Above them the terraces climb into the dusk, tier over tier, every rail lined with people, until they are too far to be people. All of it is looking down at one white uniform on the black stone. Nobody cheers. Something is thrown. It falls fast, and lands short.
She does not look up. She crouches and sets the grey shard on the ground, among the black. When she rises she is looking past the city, at the horizon. Karst looks where she looks.
A gate opens at the foot of the lowest terrace. Its stair, which has ended in air for eight hundred years, ends on the ground. Nobody comes down it. Then somebody small does.
The girl from the cathedral. Each step costs her. She has never weighed this much. On the last one she stops and looks at the ground, which is black, and has no edge.
She steps onto it.
Her legs fold. She sits down hard and puts both palms flat on the stone, as if it might move. It does not.
She looks up. Ten paces away a man with a spear and a wooden bowl is looking at her. His knuckles are white on the spear. The spear does not move.
He does not smile. He does not look away. Neither does she.
Behind her, ten thousand faces on the terraces. Behind him, an army. Nobody speaks. There is nothing yet that can be said.
WIDE, AND WIDER: the kingdom on its plain. The chains of its fleet. Beyond the Weir, Sarn Vale, green, its hearths still lit.
And on the horizon, very far and very high, in a sun that has already set down here: six more.
Signal lamps pass between them. A lone white ship, tiny at that height, is climbing toward the nearest.
CUT TO BLACK.
THE WEIGHT OF HEAVEN
